cfs.subject: scope, variable lookup and assignment rules
cfs.statement: **Scope, lookup and assignment rules.** A variable name is parsed into an optional scope qualifier (`global:`, `local:`, `script:`, `private:`) or a provider drive (`name:`), and an unqualified name. **Reading:** an unqualified name is searched in the current scope and then in each parent scope up to the global scope, and the first match wins; a variable marked `Private` is skipped when it is found in any scope other than the current one; `global:`, `local:`/`private:` and `script:` search exactly one scope (the global scope, the current scope, the script scope respectively); inside one scope the compiled locals tuple (and any dot-sourced tuples) is checked before the variable table; a drive-qualified name is read through the provider. A name that is not found yields `$null`, or a `VariableIsUndefined` error under strict mode (version 2: always; version 1: except inside expandable strings). **Writing:** an unqualified or `local:`/`private:` assignment always targets the current scope (a parent's variable of the same name is never modified; a new local variable is created if the current scope has none), `script:` and `global:` target the script and global scope; assigning to an existing variable in the target scope keeps its object and replaces its value after running its attributes (transformation, then validation), and a `ReadOnly` or `Constant` variable cannot be written (`VariableNotWritable`; `-Force` can overwrite `ReadOnly` but never `Constant`). **New scopes:** every function or script block call (not dot-sourcing) creates a child scope whose parent is the caller's scope; the script scope is the nearest enclosing scope created for a script file, or the global scope; variables marked `AllScope` are shared by reference with every new scope. **Dot-sourcing** creates no scope: the callee's locals tuple is pushed onto the current scope's `DottedScopes` for the duration of the call.
cfs.label: FACT-SRC

deviations.baseline_behavior: Values assigned to global variables are marked untrusted in Constrained Language Mode.
ExecutionContext carries language mode and invalidates binder caches on change.
